params.body:
## What

`shadow: reads beside the answer, logs what it would have done, changes nothing` in `test/ask-router.test.mjs` counted the router's call right after the answer came back. Shadow does not wait for the router, so on a slow machine the answer can end before the router's stand-in has even logged its call: CI on #401 failed there (expected 1, got 0), on a change that does not touch the router. It now waits for the router's row, which is complete only once the router has answered, and counts after.

## Checked

- The race reproduced: with the stand-in's router call held 300 ms, the test as on main fails with CI's message (expected 1, actual 0); as here it passes.
- `test/ask-router.test.mjs`: 38 of 38.

#401 (the tests' own router file) is unaffected by this and right as it is; its red CI was this race. On the box, which runs the suite before every deploy on a slower machine than the workbench, the same race could hold a deploy back.
params.title: The router's shadow test waits for the router before counting its call
